analysis.title: AI/Tech Wrecks As Crude Carnage & Macro Malaise Sparks Bond Bid, Gold Gains
key_insights: Oil fell over 7% on Nov 2, the biggest daily decline since May 20. WTI broke back below $100 to near three-week lows and Brent fell about 8% to $104. The drop followed reports that Iran's supreme leader approved pursuing negotiations, that Trump wanted to let talks play out, and a reported US-Iran breakthrough after Qatari mediation.

Bonds rallied on lower oil and weak macro, with yields down across the curve and the long end leading. The 10Y extended its move below 5.00% to its lowest in almost two months. STIRs were little changed (Dec and Jan odds flat) while 2027 rate-change expectations slipped by a few bps.
The relief bounce in big tech failed. NDX went from +1.2% near the cash open to almost -1.5%, taking out Friday's lows. QQQ fell to its 200DMA and NDX is in correction, down over 10% from its highs.

The broad AI basket fell about 3% while SPX ex-AI rose 1%. NeoClouds and optical networking stocks fell over 6%, memory and chip names erased last week's bounce, and momentum posted its lowest close since September.
Credit widened on AI supply fears. Data-center CDS surged back near record wides, hyperscaler credit spreads hit a new record wide, and IG spreads blew out as META and ORCL new issues arrived.

Macro data missed. ISM manufacturing rose but missed expectations (prices down) and S&P Global manufacturing fell but missed expectations (prices up). Construction spending fell 1.9% MoM, the biggest drop since COVID, driven by a 13.0% fall in home improvements, while data center spending rose 8.6%.

Lower yields and a dovish shift in 2027 Fed expectations pushed the dollar lower, holding at the low end of its one-month range. Gold rose toward $4,000 but did not get back to it after Friday's liquidation. Bitcoin gave back the weekend's gains.

The Treasury quarterly refunding announcement on Wednesday is in focus. Danske Bank says markets are watching forward guidance on maturity composition, including lower long-end issuance or more long-end buybacks.

Midterms are a day away, and AAPL and PLTR report earnings after the close. SPX has been up a year after every midterm since 1950, averaging about 15%. The article says higher odds of a Democratic sweep have coincided with lower AI stock prices.

crypto_views: Bitcoin gave back the weekend's recovery from the Binance hack as tech stocks fell.
risk_factors: AI funding fears across credit and equity markets, including record-wide hyperscaler spreads and data-center CDS.
Possible Democratic sweep in the midterms, which could remove the gridlock argument for equities.
Renewed Gulf escalation, given reports of ships struck near Hormuz and Saudi Arabia.
Treasury refunding guidance on long-end issuance and buybacks.
Late-day selling pressure in RTY and SPY showed rotation could not hold the market up.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum factor had its lowest close since September.
Bond-equity correlation has turned negative again over the past month, per Deutsche Bank's Steven Zeng. Bond gains may reflect investors protecting against further equity downside.
geopolitical: Iran's supreme leader approved government pursuit of negotiations, per state-run IRNA.
Trump reportedly told Israeli PM Netanyahu he wanted to let Iran talks play out, and a pool report says he said no to striking Iran after the elections.
Al Jadeed, citing a diplomatic source, reported a breakthrough in US-Iran talks after Qatari mediation overcame procedural obstacles.
UKMTO received reports of a ship struck in Hormuz and a vessel hit east of Ras Al Khafji, Saudi Arabia.
Kazakhstan temporarily halted crude flows toward Russia via the Atyrau-Samara pipeline after a drone strike. The route carried about 7.5 million tons in the first nine months of the year.
Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and the squeeze on Persian Gulf supply have pushed diesel and fuel prices higher in recent months.
US midterm elections are on Nov 3 (the note says the day after the oil drop).
